source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: N1QL() function (in-handler SQL++ execution)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a built-in Eventing JS function that lets a handler issue a SQL++ statement, used specifically as the sanctioned workaround for a restriction unique to Eventing handlers (inline SQL++ cannot mutate the handler's own source bucket).

relations.subject: eventing:n1ql-function
relations.object: inline SQL++ statement updating an Eventing handler's own source bucket
relations.evidence: Uses the _N1QL(…​)_ function to update the source bucket instead of an inline SQL++ statement because inline SQL++ is prohibited from updating the source bucket of an Eventing handler to prevent infinite recursion scenarios.

relations.subject: cloud/eventing/eventing-handler-docControlledSelfExpiry
relations.evidence: As described in [Expiration](#learn:data/expiration.adoc), if a "Bucket Max Time-To-Live" is set (specified in seconds), it is an enforced hard upper limit.

notable_absence.finding: This page's TTL offset-vs-absolute-timestamp and Bucket Max Time-To-Live semantics are generic Couchbase data-service behavior (explicitly cross-referenced out to the core Expiration doc), not an Eventing-specific concept - deliberately not minted here to avoid duplicating that other product surface. The one genuinely Eventing-specific mechanism on this page is the source-bucket-mutation-via-N1QL() workaround captured above. Also notes the recurring 'Version 7.1+ / Version 7.0+ / Version 6.X' settings-comment boilerplate, unchanged from the rest of the batch - flagging recurrence, not treating as new.

cross_component_finding: The N1QL(...) function call inside the handler is described as itself re-triggering the OnUpdate mutation it originated from ('This will cause recursion but it will be ignored since we ignore all non-zero TTLs'), an interaction between Eventing's mutation-listening model and SQL++'s DML that isn't visible from either component's docs in isolation.
